question: transfer-own-accounts-two-banks-online
rule: Faster Payments (Pay.UK) is the normal online interbank scheme; in practice funds arrive in seconds to minutes, 24/7. Legal maximum: Payment Services Regulations 2017 reg. 86(1) - payer's PSP must ensure the amount is credited to the payee's PSP 'by the end of the business day following the time of receipt of the payment order' (D+1; D+2 if paper-initiated). Since the Payment Services (Amendment) Regulations 2024 (in force 9 Oct 2024) a PSP may delay an outbound payment on reasonable suspicion of APP fraud up to 'the end of the fourth business day following the time of receipt'. Free for personal customers at the major banks (no statutory free-of-charge rule found).
uncertainty: Typical 'instant' speed is scheme practice, not law; the legal ceiling is D+1 (D+4 with fraud hold).
gameImplication: Model as instant by default; allow a rare fraud-hold delay up to 4 business days; never longer than D+1 otherwise.

question: account-switching-service
rule: CONFIRMED: Current Account Switch Service (CASS), operated by Pay.UK, voluntary scheme covering >99% of UK current accounts. 'A switch takes seven working days', backed by the Current Account Switch Guarantee; balance moved, Direct Debits/standing orders/incoming payments switched; redirection of payments to the old account for a minimum of three years. Free.
citation: Pay.UK - Current Account Switch Service; Current Account Switch Guarantee
uncertainty: Low. Voluntary industry scheme rather than statute (UK implemented PAD switching but CASS is the vehicle).
gameImplication: 7 working days from agreed start; balance and recurring payments move; old-account payments redirected for 3 years.

question: transfer-own-accounts-two-banks-online
rule: SEPA Credit Transfer / SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (euro). PSD2 Art. 83(1) (transposed by S.I. 6/2018): payee's PSP account credited 'at the latest by the end of the following business day' (D+1; +1 day for paper). EU Instant Payments Regulation (EU) 2024/886: euro-area PSPs had to be able to receive instant credit transfers by 9 Jan 2025 and send them by 9 Oct 2025; funds credited within 10 seconds, 24/7/365; charges for instant may not exceed those for standard credit transfers (from 9 Jan 2025 / 9 Oct 2025). Irish retail banks generally do not charge for online SEPA transfers on personal accounts (bank-specific).
citation: Directive (EU) 2015/2366 Art. 83; Regulation (EU) 2024/886; ECB IPR page
uncertainty: Price: IPR guarantees parity with standard transfers, not zero price; Irish personal-account fee schedules vary.
gameImplication: Instant (seconds) since Oct 2025 for euro-area countries; legal ceiling D+1 for non-instant.

rule: SEPA Credit Transfer (D+1 max under § 675s BGB, implementing PSD2 Art. 83) or SEPA Instant (Echtzeitüberweisung). Germany is euro area: under Regulation (EU) 2024/886 banks must receive instant transfers since 9 Jan 2025 and offer sending since 9 Oct 2025, crediting within 10 seconds 24/7; instant may cost no more than a standard SEPA transfer. question: account-switching-service
rule: CONFIRMED (12 Geschäftstage): Zahlungskontengesetz (ZKG) Kontowechselhilfe. § 22 ZKG: receiving bank requests information 'innerhalb von zwei Geschäftstagen' after receiving the authorisation; § 23: transferring bank sends lists 'innerhalb von fünf Geschäftstagen'; § 24: receiving bank sets up standing orders / accepts direct debits and informs payers/payees within five Geschäftstage -> 2+5+5 = 12 Geschäftstage. Information from the old bank is free; any fees must be reasonable and cost-based.
uncertainty: Low on the 12-day sum; the customer can choose a later switch date.
gameImplication: 12 business days; receiving bank does the work.

question: account-switching-service
rule: CONFIRMED (22 jours ouvrés): service d'aide à la mobilité bancaire (loi Macron 2015; art. L312-1-7 CMF), free and mandatory for the new bank. Steps: new bank requests info within 2 jours ouvrés; old bank provides 13 months of operations within 5 jours ouvrés; new bank informs creditors/debtors within 5 jours ouvrés; they have 10 jours ouvrés to update -> 22 jours ouvrés from signing the mandat de mobilité. Optional closing of the old account with balance transfer.
citation: Code monétaire et financier art. L312-1-7; economie.gouv.fr 'Comment changer de banque ?'

gameImplication: 22 working days; free.

rule: Domestic ISK transfers between Icelandic banks clear in real time through the Central Bank of Iceland's interbank system (MBK, launched 2020; small-value component MBK-Inst 'instant'); Iceland introduced a real-time small-value system (JK) in 2003. The EU Instant Payments Regulation (EU) 2024/886 is NOT yet incorporated into the EEA Agreement (EFTA factsheet: 'under scrutiny'; JCD pending) and in any case covers euro transfers only. PSD2 is transposed by Lög um greiðsluþjónustu nr. 114/2021 (D+1 maximum).

question: account-switching-service
rule: YES - PAD applies. Directive 2014/92/EU incorporated into EEA by JCD 171/2021 (in force 1 Feb 2024); transposed by Lög um greiðslureikninga nr. 5/2023 (in force 1 Mar 2023). Art. 8: receiving provider requests information within two viðskiptadagar; departing provider sends within five viðskiptadagar; receiving provider sets up recurring transfers/direct debits within five viðskiptadagar -> 12 business days (same structure as PAD Art. 10). Information from the departing provider is free ('án endurgjalds'); other switching fees must be reasonable and cost-based.
citation: Lög um greiðslureikninga nr. 5/2023, art. 8 and 10; EFTA EEA-Lex 32014L0092
uncertainty: Day count read via machine translation of the Icelandic text; sum (12) is derived, not stated.
gameImplication: ~12 business days, PAD-style.

question: transfer-own-accounts-two-banks-online
rule: Zengin System (Zengin-Net), Japan's retail interbank credit-transfer system, relays transfers in real time: during Core Time (weekdays ~8:30-15:30) the receiving account is credited immediately; since Oct 2018 the 'More Time' system extends this to 24/7 for participating banks. Outside a non-participating bank's hours, credit is next business day. Not free by default: inter-bank transfer fees (furikomi tesūryō) are set by each bank, commonly a few hundred yen online, with net banks offering some free transfers per month.
uncertainty: More Time participation is per bank; no statutory D+1 maximum found. Fee levels not taken from an official tariff here.
gameImplication: Instant in most cases, next business day if a bank is outside its hours; charge a small transfer fee.

question: account-switching-service
rule: YES: 계좌이동서비스 (Payinfo, operated by KFTC, launched 2015). Lets customers look up, cancel or move to another account their 자동납부 (biller-pulled automatic payments: telecom, insurance, card bills, etc.) and 자동송금 (customer-set recurring transfers). It moves the payment instructions, not the balance. Payinfo: results confirmed 'up to 5 business days after the application date (excluding that day)'; 자동송금 changes take effect immediately; users are told to apply at least 6 business days before the next debit date. (Separately, 계좌통합관리 lets customers close small dormant accounts and move their balance.)
uncertainty: Day count quoted via bank pages relaying Payinfo; balance-move caps of 계좌통합관리 not verified.
gameImplication: Recurring payments move in <=5 business days (transfers instant); balance moved separately by the player.

rule: SPEI (Banco de México), available 24/7/365. Banxico SPEI rules (Circular 14/2017 as amended) require the beneficiary participant to credit the client's account within 5 or 30 seconds depending on participant type; the sending participant must submit the order within 30 seconds of telling the client it was accepted. Typical arrival: seconds. Many banks do not charge for SPEI through digital channels, but fees are bank-set.
